title: Explanatio Psalmorum XII
author: Ambrose
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0022.stoa048.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.

passages.original: qui cum refugeret apostolum se scribere, seniorem scripsit nec minor est aestimatus, cui cygnea quaedam suppeteret gratia senectutis. ipse uas electionis dominicae scribens ad Philemonem ait: cumsis talis utPaulus senex, nunc autem et uinctus Christi Iesu, obsecro te pro meo filio, quem genui in uinculis, Onesimo. uolens itaque illi plurimum deferre seniori Paulo eum, non iuueni
passages.english: He, though he shrank from writing himself an apostle, wrote [himself] "the elder," and was not thought the less for it, since a certain swan-like grace of old age was at his command. The very vessel of the Lord's election, writing to Philemon, says: "Since you are such a one as Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus, I beseech you for my son, whom I begot in chains, Onesimus." And so, wishing to defer very greatly to him [he likened] him to the elder Paul, not to the young
passages.notes: "cumsis talis utPaulus" is read as "cum sis talis ut Paulus" (scanning error). The subject of the first sentence is presumably John, who calls himself "the elder" (presbyter) in his letters; the context is not given. The final sentence breaks off and its construction is incomplete. "[he likened]" is a conjectural supplement to make sense of the accusative "eum".
